[Feature]

### Objective

Provide a dependency-free TypeScript module that renders multiple analog clock faces as a single standalone SVG document, one clock per requested IANA timezone, so a reader can see the current time across several regions at a glance.

The module is a pure rendering library: callers supply the instant to render, and the module returns SVG markup. This keeps output deterministic and fully testable under Node's built-in test runner.

### Acceptance Criteria

Time conversion

REQ-1: Given a UTC instant and an IANA timezone identifier, the module resolves the local hour (0–23), minute, and second in that zone.
REQ-2: Zones with non-integer UTC offsets resolve correctly, verified for Asia/Kolkata (+05:30), Asia/Kathmandu (+05:45), and Australia/Eucla (+08:45).
REQ-3: Daylight saving transitions resolve correctly, verified for the same instant rendered in America/New_York and Europe/London on dates either side of a transition.
REQ-4: An unrecognised timezone identifier throws an error naming the offending identifier. The error is thrown, not swallowed or defaulted to UTC.

Hand geometry

REQ-5: The second hand is at seconds × 6 degrees clockwise from twelve.
REQ-6: The minute hand is at minutes × 6 + seconds × 0.1 degrees, so it advances smoothly within the minute.
REQ-7: The hour hand is at (hour mod 12) × 30 + minutes × 0.5 degrees, so 6:30 local time places it midway between 6 and 7.
REQ-8: Local midnight and local noon both place the hour hand at 0 degrees.
REQ-9: All returned angles are normalised to the range [0, 360).

Rendering

REQ-10: Rendering one clock returns an SVG group containing a circular face, twelve hour ticks, three hands, and a text label showing the timezone.
REQ-11: Rendering a list of timezones returns one complete, well-formed SVG document containing exactly one clock group per entry, laid out left to right in the order supplied.
REQ-12: The same (instant, timezone list) pair always produces byte-identical output.
REQ-13: Timezone labels are escaped so that &, <, and > cannot break out of the SVG text element.
REQ-14: An empty timezone list returns a valid empty SVG document rather than throwing.
REQ-15: A duplicated timezone in the list renders that clock once per occurrence.

### Constraints and Non-goals

Hard constraints — the change is rejected if any are violated

No new runtime or development dependencies. package.json and package-lock.json are protected paths. Use Node built-ins only; resolve timezones with Intl.DateTimeFormat and formatToParts, not a vendored timezone database.
All new source goes under src/worldclock/. Top-level src/*.ts and tsconfig.json are protected and must not be modified.
All new tests go under test and match test/**/*.test.ts.
No binary files. SVG is emitted as text; no PNG, ICO, or font assets.
Overall coverage must not drop. The baseline is 90.77% lines and 85.66% branches with a permitted drop of zero, so every new branch — including each error path — needs a test.
Rendering functions must be pure: no Date.now(), no process.env, no file, network, or console I/O. The instant is always a parameter.
Scope must fit six tasks or fewer.

Non-goals

No browser application, framework, bundler, or build step.
No live ticking, animation, or setInterval.
No CLI entry point. An uncovered entry module would breach the coverage gate.
No persistence, configuration files, user preferences, or network calls.
No digital time display, no date display, no analog/digital toggle.

### Context

Follow the existing module conventions in lifecycle.ts and the test style in lifecycle.test.ts, including .ts extensions on relative imports.
Budgets and protected paths are defined in policy.json.
Verification runs via npm run verify.

# Plan: Multi-Timezone Analog Clock SVG Renderer

## Summary

Add a dependency-free module under `src/worldclock/` that converts a UTC
instant to local hour/minute/second for arbitrary IANA timezones using
`Intl.DateTimeFormat` + `formatToParts`, computes analog clock hand angles,
and renders one or more clock faces as a single deterministic SVG document.
Tests live under `test/**/*.test.ts` using `node --test`, matching the style
of `lifecycle.ts` / `lifecycle.test.ts` (`.ts` extensions on relative imports,
plain `assert.equal`/`assert.throws`).

## Rebase status (this revision)

Re-verified against the current default branch: `origin/main` HEAD is
`f7ba26ca1746da28a354542f7e344029cec8d7c6`, identical to this job's
`baseSha`/`headSha`/`controlSha`. The branch is already current with `main`;
no rebase conflicts exist and no commits need replaying. Scope, task names,
and design below are unchanged from plan v2 per the requester's feedback:
keep exactly the four tasks `worldclock-time`, `worldclock-geometry`,
`worldclock-render-single`, `worldclock-render-document`; no Playwright; no
new dependencies.

## Sources consulted

- `source/src/lifecycle.ts`, `source/test/lifecycle.test.ts` — existing module
  and test conventions (named exports, `.ts` import extensions, `node:assert/strict`).
- `source/package.json` — confirms Node ≥24.8, `type: module`, no bundler; test
  script is `node --test 'test/**/*.test.ts'`; coverage via c8 with thresholds
  lines 80% / branches 70% (repo-wide `npm run verify`); issue text states a
  stricter baseline of 90.77%/85.66% with zero permitted drop — the new module
  must be near-fully covered. No `playwright` dependency or reference exists
  anywhere in the repository (`package.json`, source, tests) — confirmed by
  search; nothing to remove and no risk of reintroducing it.
- `source/tsconfig.json` — `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`,
  `verbatimModuleSyntax`, NodeNext resolution; confirms `src/*.ts` at the
  top level is protected, but `src/worldclock/**` is not.
- `.sdlc-context.json` policy — protected paths include `src/*.ts` and
  `tsconfig.json` (top-level only, glob is non-recursive), so a subdirectory
  `src/worldclock/` is safe to add; `package.json`/`package-lock.json` are
  protected, confirming no new dependencies are possible or needed.
- Re-verified live with Node 24.20 in this environment (no vendored tz data,
  no third-party packages):
  - `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone, hour:'numeric', minute:'numeric', second:'numeric', hourCycle:'h23' }).formatToParts(date)`
    yields exact local h/m/s for fractional-offset zones: for the instant
    `2024-03-10T07:00:00Z`, Asia/Kolkata → `12:30:00` (+05:30), Asia/Kathmandu
    → `12:45:00` (+05:45), Australia/Eucla → `15:45:00` (+08:45).
  - An unknown zone id (e.g. `Not/AZone`) throws
    `RangeError: Invalid time zone specified: Not/AZone` synchronously at
    `Intl.DateTimeFormat` construction — this can be caught and rethrown with
    the offending identifier embedded, satisfying REQ-4.
  - America/New_York DST spring-forward: for the instant `2024-03-10T07:00:00Z`
    (before the 2am local transition on the US east coast), America/New_York
    resolves to `03:00:00` (having jumped from 01:59 to 03:00 at 07:00 UTC)
    while Europe/London resolves to `07:00:00` in the same call — confirming
    the API handles DST transitions correctly without extra logic (REQ-3).

## Proposed design

`src/worldclock/` (new directory, 4 files, one per task below):

1. **`time.ts`** (task `worldclock-time`) —
   `resolveLocalTime(instant: Date, timeZone: string): { hour: number; minute: number; second: number }`.
   Builds `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `hourCycle: 'h23'` so hour is 0–23
   (`h23` avoids the "24" midnight quirk of default `h24`), reads parts via
   `formatToParts`, parses hour/minute/second as integers. Wraps the
   `Intl.DateTimeFormat` constructor and format call in try/catch; on failure,
   throws `new Error(\`Unrecognised timezone: ${timeZone}\`)` including the
   original identifier (REQ-1, REQ-4).

2. **`geometry.ts`** (task `worldclock-geometry`) — pure angle functions, each
   normalising into `[0, 360)` via `((deg % 360) + 360) % 360` (REQ-9):
   - `secondHandAngle(second): number` → `second * 6` (REQ-5)
   - `minuteHandAngle(minute, second): number` → `minute * 6 + second * 0.1` (REQ-6)
   - `hourHandAngle(hour, minute): number` → `(hour % 12) * 30 + minute * 0.5`
     (REQ-7; hour 0 and hour 12 both → `0 * 30 = 0`, satisfying REQ-8 for
     midnight/noon when minute is 0 — note REQ-8 only requires this holding
     when minutes are exactly on the hour, which is how the acceptance test
     will be written, consistent with the existing formula in REQ-7).

3. **`render.ts`** (task `worldclock-render-single`) — SVG string builders for
   a single clock, no I/O, pure functions of their arguments only (no
   `Date.now()`, `process.env`, file/network/console):
   - `escapeXml(value: string): string` replaces `&`, `<`, `>` (and for safety
     `"`/`'` since they appear in attributes too) with entities (REQ-13).
   - `renderClock(instant: Date, timeZone: string, x: number): string` — calls
     `resolveLocalTime` + geometry functions, returns a `<g transform="translate(x,0)">`
     containing: a `<circle>` face, twelve `<line>` hour ticks (fixed, at
     30°-step positions, unaffected by input, but present in every clock per
     REQ-10), three `<line>` hands (hour/minute/second) positioned by the
     computed angles via trig (`Math.sin`/`Math.cos` with angle-from-twelve
     convention: `x = r*sin(θ)`, `y = -r*cos(θ)`), and a `<text>` label with
     the escaped timezone id (REQ-10, REQ-13).

4. **`document.ts`** (task `worldclock-render-document`) —
   `renderClocks(instant: Date, timeZones: string[], options?): string` —
   maps `timeZones` left-to-right into fixed-width `renderClock` groups
   (duplicates render independently and identically, REQ-15), joins them,
   and wraps in one `<svg width=... height=...>...</svg>` root with a fixed
   viewBox sized to `timeZones.length` (REQ-11). Empty array still returns
   a well-formed `<svg>` root with no groups (REQ-14). All dimensions are
   constants/derived only from `timeZones.length` and array order, and all
   numeric formatting uses a fixed-precision helper (e.g. round to 3
   decimals) so floating point angle computation is byte-identical across
   runs for the same input (REQ-12).

No barrel/`index.ts` file is planned: this keeps the scope to exactly the
four approved tasks and avoids adding an export surface beyond what each task
needs; tests import directly from `src/worldclock/time.ts`,
`src/worldclock/geometry.ts`, `src/worldclock/render.ts`, and
`src/worldclock/document.ts`, mirroring how existing `src/*.ts` modules are
imported directly elsewhere in the repo.

## Alternatives considered

- **Vendoring a timezone database** — rejected outright: forbidden by the
  hard constraint and unnecessary since `Intl` + `formatToParts` already
  gives correct, DST-aware conversions per the verification above.
- **Using `hourCycle: 'h24'`** (idiomatic default in many locales) — rejected;
  `h24` reports local midnight as `"24"` not `"0"`, which would need extra
  normalisation. `h23` returns `0-23` directly, matching REQ-1 with no post-processing.
- **Computing hand angles from a `Date` object with local wall-clock getters**
  (e.g. constructing a `Date` shifted by offset) — rejected in favor of
  deriving hour/minute/second directly from `formatToParts` integers; avoids
  subtle rounding/DST edge cases from date arithmetic and keeps `resolveLocalTime`
  the single source of truth for time conversion, independently testable
  against REQ-1–REQ-4.
- **One `<svg>` per clock, concatenated as sibling documents** — rejected;
  REQ-11 requires "one complete, well-formed SVG document" for the whole
  list, so a single root `<svg>` with per-clock `<g>` children is required.
- **Browser-based rendering or Playwright screenshot testing of the SVG
  output** — explicitly rejected per requester feedback: this is a pure,
  dependency-free string-rendering library; no browser, headless or
  otherwise, and no new dev dependency (Playwright or any other) is
  introduced or required to validate the output. Tests assert on the
  returned SVG markup string directly (substring/structure checks), which is
  sufficient for every REQ and keeps `package.json`/`package-lock.json`
  untouched.
- **A five/sixth task for a barrel `index.ts` or extra polish** — held in
  reserve but not scheduled; the four tasks above are sufficient to satisfy
  every REQ and the requester's feedback keeps the scope at exactly these
  four.

## Non-goals confirmed unaffected

No ticking/animation, no CLI, no persistence/network, no digital time or date
display, no browser bundle — the design above introduces none of these. No
Playwright or any other new dependency is added.

## Test/validation strategy

New tests under `test/worldclock/*.test.ts` (or flat `test/worldclock.*.test.ts`,
matching `test/**/*.test.ts`), using `node:assert/strict` + `node:test`,
mirroring `lifecycle.test.ts` style:

- Time conversion (`worldclock-time`): exact h/m/s for Asia/Kolkata, Asia/Kathmandu,
  Australia/Eucla against known UTC instants; New_York/London DST
  before/after a documented transition instant; invalid zone id throws with
  the id in the message (REQ-1–4).
- Geometry (`worldclock-geometry`): table-driven cases for each formula at boundary inputs (0, and
  values that would exceed 360° before normalisation) confirming range
  `[0,360)` and the exact documented formulas, plus explicit midnight/noon
  hour-hand-at-0 case (REQ-5–9).
- Single-clock rendering (`worldclock-render-single`): `renderClock` output contains exactly one `<circle>`, twelve tick
  `<line>`s, three hand `<line>`s (or equivalent identifiable path/line
  count), and the escaped label text; a `&`/`<`/`>`-containing timezone-like
  string used in a label (or a synthetic case) confirms escaping (REQ-10, REQ-13).
- Document assembly (`worldclock-render-document`): `renderClocks` produces one group per
  input in supplied order including a duplicate case and an empty-list case
  returning a valid `<svg>...</svg>` shell; calling
  `renderClocks` twice with identical inputs asserts `===` string equality
  (REQ-11, REQ-12, REQ-14, REQ-15).
- No `Date.now()`/env/IO used anywhere in `src/worldclock/`; all functions
  take the instant as an explicit parameter, verified structurally by
  passing a fixed literal `Date` in every test and by code review during the
  code stage.
- Run via existing `npm run verify` (typecheck → `test:coverage` with c8 →
  build); no script or coverage-config changes needed since c8 is already
  configured to include `src/**/*.ts` and the test runner already globs
  `test/**/*.test.ts`. No Playwright or other new dev dependency is added or
  required.

## Security considerations

- Pure computation only; no untrusted input crosses a privilege boundary.
  Timezone strings are user-supplied but only ever passed to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`,
  which is a bounded, no-I/O built-in — malformed input is rejected via a
  thrown `RangeError`/`Error`, never executed or interpolated into anything
  beyond escaped SVG text.
- `escapeXml` prevents label content from breaking out of the SVG `<text>`
  element or attributes (REQ-13), mitigating injection into any downstream
  consumer that renders the returned SVG string as markup (e.g. embedding in
  HTML).
- No dependency surface added — nothing to audit beyond the new source and
  test files themselves.

## Task breakdown (finalized per requester feedback, unchanged from plan v2)

Exactly four tasks, fitting within the 6-task policy limit:

1. `worldclock-time` — `src/worldclock/time.ts`: `resolveLocalTime` and the
   unrecognised-timezone error path (REQ-1–4). No dependencies.
2. `worldclock-geometry` — `src/worldclock/geometry.ts`: hand-angle formulas
   and normalisation (REQ-5–9). No dependencies (independent of task 1).
3. `worldclock-render-single` — `src/worldclock/render.ts`: single-clock SVG
   group rendering, ticks, hands, label, and `escapeXml` (REQ-10, REQ-13).
   Depends on `worldclock-time` and `worldclock-geometry`.
4. `worldclock-render-document` — `src/worldclock/document.ts`: multi-clock
   document assembly, ordering, duplicates, empty list, determinism
   (REQ-11, REQ-12, REQ-14, REQ-15). Depends on `worldclock-render-single`.

## Unresolved questions

- REQ-8 says "local midnight and local noon both place the hour hand at 0
  degrees" — the REQ-7 formula `(hour % 12) * 30 + minute * 0.5` only yields
  exactly 0° at minute 0. Should the acceptance test for REQ-8 be interpreted
  strictly at `minute === 0` (consistent with REQ-7's own worked example,
  "6:30 ... midway between 6 and 7"), or is there an expectation of a
  separate zero-minute-offset rule for hour 0/12 specifically? I've assumed
  the former (test only at exact midnight/noon, i.e. minute=second=0) since
  it's the only interpretation consistent with REQ-7's formula; please
  confirm or clarify before coding if a different behavior was intended.
  (Carried over unresolved from plan v2; not addressed by this revision's
  feedback, which only concerned rebase/scope/Playwright.)
- No other blocking ambiguities found; sizing, dependency, and protected-path
  constraints are all satisfiable as scoped above.

tasks.title: Implement timezone-aware local time resolution
tasks.description: Create src/worldclock/time.ts exporting resolveLocalTime(instant: Date, timeZone: string): { hour: number; minute: number; second: number }. Use Intl.DateTimeFormat with hourCycle: 'h23' and formatToParts to derive local hour (0-23), minute, and second from a UTC instant and an IANA timezone identifier. Do not use Date.now(), process.env, or any file/network/console I/O; the instant is always an explicit parameter. Wrap Intl.DateTimeFormat construction/formatting in a try/catch and on failure throw a new Error naming the offending timezone identifier (do not default to UTC or swallow the error). Follow the module conventions in src/lifecycle.ts (named exports, .ts extensions on relative imports, strict TypeScript). Add tests under test/worldclock/time.test.ts (or test/worldclock.time.test.ts) using node:assert/strict and node:test, mirroring test/lifecycle.test.ts style.
acceptance: REQ-1: Given a UTC instant and IANA timezone, resolveLocalTime returns correct local hour (0-23), minute, and second.
REQ-2: Fractional UTC-offset zones resolve correctly: verified with test cases for Asia/Kolkata (+05:30), Asia/Kathmandu (+05:45), and Australia/Eucla (+08:45).
REQ-3: DST transitions resolve correctly: verified for the same instant rendered in America/New_York and Europe/London on dates either side of a transition.
REQ-4: An unrecognised timezone identifier causes resolveLocalTime to throw an Error whose message includes the offending identifier; the error is not swallowed or defaulted to UTC.
resolveLocalTime contains no Date.now(), process.env, or file/network/console I/O; the instant is always taken as a parameter.
New tests live under test/**/*.test.ts and do not modify any existing baseline test.

tasks.title: Implement clock hand angle geometry functions
tasks.description: Create src/worldclock/geometry.ts exporting pure functions secondHandAngle(second: number): number, minuteHandAngle(minute: number, second: number): number, and hourHandAngle(hour: number, minute: number): number. Each function computes the documented formula and normalises the result into the range [0, 360) using ((deg % 360) + 360) % 360. No I/O or side effects. Add tests under test/worldclock/geometry.test.ts (or test/worldclock.geometry.test.ts) covering boundary and wrap-around inputs.
acceptance: REQ-5: secondHandAngle(second) equals second * 6 degrees clockwise from twelve, normalised to [0, 360).
REQ-6: minuteHandAngle(minute, second) equals minute * 6 + second * 0.1 degrees, normalised to [0, 360).
REQ-7: hourHandAngle(hour, minute) equals (hour % 12) * 30 + minute * 0.5 degrees, e.g. hour=6, minute=30 yields a value midway between the 6 and 7 hour positions, normalised to [0, 360).
REQ-8: hourHandAngle at local midnight (hour=0, minute=0) and local noon (hour=12, minute=0) both return 0 degrees.
REQ-9: All three functions return angles strictly within [0, 360) for inputs that would otherwise exceed or reach 360 or be negative before normalisation.
New tests live under test/**/*.test.ts and do not modify any existing baseline test.

tasks.title: Render a single analog clock face as an SVG group
tasks.description: Create src/worldclock/render.ts exporting escapeXml(value: string): string and renderClock(instant: Date, timeZone: string, x: number): string. escapeXml must replace &, <, and > (and, defensively, " and ') with entity references so a timezone label cannot break out of SVG text/attribute context. renderClock must call resolveLocalTime (from worldclock-time) and the geometry functions (from worldclock-geometry) to build a <g transform="translate(x,0)"> containing: one circular face (<circle>), twelve fixed hour-tick <line> elements, three hand <line> elements (hour, minute, second) positioned via trigonometry from the computed angles, and a <text> element with the escaped timezone label. renderClock must be pure: no Date.now(), process.env, or file/network/console I/O; instant and timeZone are explicit parameters, and numeric output must use a fixed-precision formatting helper so results are deterministic. Add tests under test/worldclock/render.test.ts (or test/worldclock.render.test.ts).
acceptance: REQ-10: renderClock returns an SVG group containing exactly one <circle> face, twelve hour-tick <line>s, three hand <line>s, and one <text> label showing the timezone identifier.

REQ-13: A timezone label containing &, <, or > is escaped by escapeXml so the characters cannot break out of the SVG <text> element; a test exercises escapeXml directly and/or via a label containing these characters.
renderClock and escapeXml use no Date.now(), process.env, or file/network/console I/O.
Calling renderClock twice with identical (instant, timeZone, x) arguments returns byte-identical output.
New tests live under test/**/*.test.ts and do not modify any existing baseline test.

tasks.title: Assemble multi-timezone clocks into one SVG document
tasks.description: Create src/worldclock/document.ts exporting renderClocks(instant: Date, timeZones: string[]): string. It must map timeZones left-to-right into renderClock groups (from worldclock-render-single) at increasing fixed x-offsets, join them, and wrap the result in a single well-formed root <svg ...>...</svg> element sized deterministically from timeZones.length. Duplicated timezone identifiers in the list must render independently, once per occurrence, in the supplied order. An empty timeZones array must return a valid, well-formed empty <svg> document (an <svg> root with no clock groups) rather than throwing. All output must be deterministic: no Date.now(), process.env, or file/network/console I/O, and identical (instant, timeZones) input must produce byte-identical (=== equal) string output across calls. Add tests under test/worldclock/document.test.ts (or test/worldclock.document.test.ts).
acceptance: REQ-11: renderClocks returns one complete, well-formed SVG document containing exactly one clock group per entry in timeZones, laid out left to right in the order supplied.
REQ-12: Calling renderClocks twice with the same (instant, timeZones) arguments produces byte-identical (=== equal) string output.
REQ-14: renderClocks([]) (or an empty timeZones array for any instant) returns a valid, well-formed SVG document with no clock groups, without throwing.
REQ-15: A timeZones list containing a duplicated timezone identifier renders that clock once per occurrence, each in its correct left-to-right position.
renderClocks uses no Date.now(), process.env, or file/network/console I/O.
New tests live under test/**/*.test.ts and do not modify any existing baseline test.
